title: Coefficient associativity of normalized tensor inverse image
statement:
The canonical tensor/pullback comparisons commute with coefficient association, without boundedness or flatness assumptions. The functors are those of [det-sp-scalar-extension-functor] and [lem-fix-direct-image-scalar-exchange].

theorem directImageScalarPullbackCoefficientCocycle
    {A B C : Type u} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [CommRing C]
    [Finite A] [Finite B] [Finite C] (φ : A →+* B) (ψ : B →+* C)
    {Z Y : Scheme.{u}} (p : Z ⟶ Y) (K : proEtaleDerivedCategory Y A) :
    (proEtaleConstantRingDerivedPullback C p).map
        ((scalarExtensionFunctor_composition φ ψ Y).hom.app K) ≫
      (directImageScalarPullbackIso (ψ.comp φ) p).hom.app K =
    (directImageScalarPullbackIso ψ p).hom.app ((scalarExtensionFunctor φ Y).obj K) ≫
      (scalarExtensionFunctor ψ Z).map ((directImageScalarPullbackIso φ p).hom.app K) ≫
        (scalarExtensionFunctor_composition φ ψ Z).hom.app
          ((proEtaleConstantRingDerivedPullback A p).obj K)

proof.text: On flat-term K-flat models, compute the composite scalar-adjunction unit: the balanced associator multiplies the two inserted units, hence preserves the composite unit. The universal derived counits and exact restriction quotient factorizations descend this equation. The unit equation identifies scalarExtensionFunctor_composition with the leftAdjointCompIso for the derived scalar adjunctions. On the right-adjoint side, restriction/direct-image coefficient squares compose because their ordinary components are identity on sections. Exact derived descent and successive conjugate mate pasting transfer this equality first to restriction/pullback and then to scalar/pullback, with the scalar associators just identified. Cancel the invertible components to obtain the displayed cocycle.
